lines.en: Wrapped in a faint light that warmed his entire body, the Wenny King dreamed, curled up like a fetus.
It was a very old dream. A story from before his ■■ had even been decided.
He lay in a polluted forest.
―Ypsilon! Just a little farther. We're almost at the Demon King's castle!
In that story, he was a hero on a quest to slay the Demon King. A hero who had set out on an expedition against the Demon King to protect the world.
But he never fulfilled that long-cherished wish. Just before the Demon King could be defeated, he closed his eyes while looking at his dear friend.
―······Gilbert.
The scene changed. This time, the setting was a battlefield.
He was a martial artist dressed in black night gear.
―Senior Brother Gwak! The Demon Cult bastards' stronghold is right over there!
His companion's face filled his entire field of vision. An aching longing welled up within him.
The one person he had loved most in that entire life.
―······It's already too late for me. Junior Sister, go on ahead.
With the sound of an arrow flying from somewhere, his vision went dark again.
His head throbbed. Amid the flood of memories, the Wenny King's sense of self was wavering.
Were these his memories, or the story of the 「Final Wall」?
Where did this story begin, and where did it end?
Regardless of his wishes, the story continued.
He was a young hatchling.
A monster of an unknown species.
He was a master of Murim, or a medieval knight.
Each time, he was an incarnation carrying out scenarios.
The last thing he heard in front of the [Final Wall] was the voice of an unknown shadow.
―My friend, stay with me in our next life, too.
He opened his eyes with a gasp, and pitch-black darkness seeped into them. The cold sweat soaking the back of his neck made him shiver.
'I am the Wenny King.'
That was his name. He had a separate true name, but he had forgotten it long ago. No, he could no longer even be certain that it really was his name.
'······Am I really the Wenny King?'
In the black, swirling vacuum, the Wenny King sank into deep thought.
It was a question he had never considered since escaping mortality.
'Who am I?'
The Stories supporting his existence were wavering.
He sifted through his memories, desperate to recover himself somehow.
「In the beginning, there was a Wenny man.」
「He was the first storyteller. A human who sang Stories.」
「Then one day, dokkaebis appeared in the world.」
「And the dokkaebis took the Wenny man's song.」
That was all he needed to remember.
The damned dokkaebis had taken the Wenny man's song. By stealing his Story of origin, they had banished him from the scenarios of the <Star Stream>.
[You look confused, my old friend.]
At the True Voice, the Wenny King whirled around in alarm.
The Dokkaebi King's face floated in the pitch darkness.
[Dokkaebi King!]
The Wenny King growled and released his Status. But it did not work properly. In the empty void, the Status he released left only faint sparks.
The Dokkaebi King spoke indifferently.
[We cannot fight here. Our powers do not work in this place.]
[······So you managed to survive. I thought the puppet's sword had killed you.]
[I am as good as dead already. And I will die again.]
Where the Dokkaebi King was looking, there was a circular exit of swirling light.
The two beings' soul bodies were moving slowly toward it.
The Wenny King shouted.
[No, my Story is only beginning. I am going beyond the 'Final Wall' now. I will face the lazy god who imagined all these worlds, and become the only one who knows this world's secret!]
[Are you so curious about the world's secret?]
[You state the obvious. Every being is curious about its own birth.]
[And that is precisely why beings become unhappy.]
The Dokkaebi King spoke as though mocking himself.
[Why do you think beings were given that welcome ability called 'forgetting'?]
Fragments of Stories scattered through the darkness. Stories that had lost their context crumbled into heaps of letters.
They were stories no one could read anymore.
The Dokkaebi King stroked them, then crushed the Stories.
[There are too many unnecessary stories in this universe. It needs a process to remove them all and optimize it. That is 'forgetting.']
[Nonsense! The universe is infinite. Just as the 'Final Wall' has no end.]
[However much blank space the Wall may have, how much do you think is allotted to a mere extra?]
The Dokkaebi King looked down at his slowly crumbling body.
[Unfortunately, the 'Final Wall' chose neither you nor me as its protagonist.]
[I don't know what nonsense you're talking about······!]
[Still, you will soon meet the being you seek.]
At those words, the Wenny King's shoulders twitched.
He could see the exit of light. A dazzling, entrancing radiance. Spinning fiercely, the exit looked like the final period of some world.
The Wenny King grew afraid.
[Have you ever seen what lies beyond?]
The Dokkaebi King did not answer immediately. He looked bored, as though every sentence after the final period were meaningless. But in the end, he added an unnecessary remark.
[What meaning would that have?]
[What?]
[I mean, what use would it be to learn that this world is a fragment of a faraway dream?]
His words held a profound emptiness.
The Wenny King could not understand them.
Even as the light grew brighter, the Dokkaebi King's expression grew dimmer.
The exit was right before them now. Uneasy, the Wenny King asked.
[······Why have you kept the <Star Stream> going all this time?]
Had the question caught him off guard? The Dokkaebi King's expression changed strangely. He gazed at the Wenny King, then answered.
[Who knows. I've forgotten.]
At that moment, several Stories overlapped on the Dokkaebi King's face.
He looked like a hero slaying the Demon King, a master of the Murim Alliance fighting the Demon Cult, and a hatchling beating its wings toward the blue sky. He was······.
[You―]
[Kim Dokja opened a door that should never have been opened. This world will be unhappy forever now.]
With those words, light enveloped the world. They had finally reached the exit.
The Wenny King staggered into the light. He pushed through its rays, little by little.
The answer was here.
The 'Oldest Dream' that had created this world was here.
But the Wenny man could see nothing.
Somewhere, a horn blared. An acrid smell stung his nose. Breathing grew harder and harder. His body was burning in the light.
As though this blank space had never been permitted to him.
[I told you. This is not your story or mine.]
At the Dokkaebi King's words, the Wenny King's body began to melt.
[We are merely tools of this world.]
Even as his legs and torso melted away, the Wenny King did not take his eyes off the sight before him.
An ancient dream was over there. Every secret of this world was there.
Something he had searched for forever was there.
The Wenny King saw it. And he understood what the Dokkaebi King had said.
That was, that really was······.
The Wenny King desperately wanted to cry out. Look this way. Please, I am here. Meet my eyes, just once.
Then its head slowly turned.
But by the time its gaze finally reached the Wenny King, he was no longer there.
It looked away again.
Then it lowered its head and became absorbed in something once more.
I coughed and felt something rough inside my mouth. When I released my pent-up breath, something like insects spilled out. Looking closely, I saw they were letters.
My senses returned, and my vision gradually brightened. Letters shone white before my eyes. The words were familiar.
Where in the world······.
“Dokja-ssi? You'll get sucked into that book at this rate.”

A chill ran down my neck. A familiar voice. Words I had heard somewhere before. A terrible possibility tore through my head. I had once thought that something like that might happen if we broke the [Final Wall]. But could it really―
Torn pages fluttered before my eyes.
Looking more closely, I realized someone was waving a book in front of me.
“······Sangah-ssi.”
Yoo Sangah was right in front of me.
Little by little, I took in my surroundings. Heaps of scattered books, and the tightly packed shelves of the library.
Faint lamplight. This was not the subway.
It was a place I knew well.
Yoo Sangah smiled brightly.
“This place feels cozy now.”
We were inside the [Fourth Wall].
“······What happened?”
“I couldn't tell you······ Actually, I only just woke up myself. Should we look for the senior librarians?”
While Yoo Sangah shrugged and looked around, I quickly reviewed what had happened to me.
「We gathered every fragment of the [Final Wall]. And at last, we broke the Wall.」
The memory of that swirling 'square circle' was still vivid.
······And? What on earth happened after that?
What about the others?
「Don't wor ry Kim Dok ja」
A voice I had thought I would never hear again.
I shouted in delight.
“Fourth Wall!”
「Qui et in the lib rary」
Even its glibness was familiar. This was unmistakably the [Fourth Wall] I remembered.
But delight aside, my questions only grew.
Why on earth was I inside the [Fourth Wall] now?
“Dokja-ssi?”
One by one, voices came out of the darkness.
They were the members of <Kim Dokja's Company>.
“Where on earth are we?”
“······Found a weird book. 『Kim Dokja and the Mystery of Sex』.”
“You shouldn't just go looking at things like that, Jihye.”
“Then what about this? 『If They Have the Bible, Kim Dokja Has Ways of Survival』.”
“Do you really want to read that?”
As Jung Heewon and Lee Jihye's voices alternated, little heads suddenly poked out of a nearby heap of books like moles.
“Ajusshi!”
“Hyung!”
Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung. In the dim light, I also saw Han Sooyoung walking toward us.
“They've got everything in here. Is this the 'library' Yoo Sangah talked about?”
Han Sooyoung pulled books from the shelves one by one and tossed them behind her. Standing behind her, Lee Hyunsung hurriedly caught them and gathered them in his arms.
“S-Sooyoung-ssi! You can't handle books so carelessly······ We don't even know what these are!”
“Hey, what's this? Looks fun.”
Behind them lay the unconscious Gong Pildu, Jang Hayoung, and Anna Croft in a row. Lee Seolhwa was checking their pulses.
At least everyone who had entered the 'Final Scenario' seemed to be here.
「Not eve ryone」
The [Fourth Wall]'s voice gave me a sense of foreboding.
There was someone I still couldn't see.
······Surely not?
「(Hahahaha! Yoo Joonghyuk! I smell Yoo Joonghyuk somewhere! Have you finally come to become one with me!)」

The voice boomed through the deep darkness. Needless to say, it was Nirvana's. A moment later, a dull thud rang out. Nirvana fell silent and rolled limply across the floor. I saw the black combat boot that had stomped on their head.
“······An unpleasant place.”
“Yoo Joonghyuk.”
Faint sparks still flowed from him, as though he had not yet separated from the 'Secretive Plotter'.
Then who exactly were the ones who hadn't made it here?
“······The constellations aren't here.”
“What happened to the people on Earth?”
The fact that the [Fourth Wall] had evacuated us here meant something had gone wrong outside.
My heart went cold. I remembered the [Fourth Wall] shattering, the sentences scattering across it. What had gone wrong? Had I destroyed the world by trying to change the story?
Then the [Fourth Wall] suddenly said something unexpected.
「Time sim ply isn't flow ing be cause no one reads or ima gines」
Before I could ask what it meant, someone appeared.
「(Have you finally broken the Wall, Apostle of Eternity and the Final Chapter?)」
「(······So this day really did come in the end.)」
They were the library's librarians, the 'Eater of Dreams' and 'Simulation'.
I looked at them, then spoke to the [Fourth Wall].
“Let me out again. There's something I need to check.”
The librarians answered.
「(Even you will not be safe if you go outside now. The <Star Stream> is gone. Everything out there has stopped.)」
Everything had stopped.
Indeed, the Stories I had heard through the Wall were no longer audible.
Instead, I heard something like an enormous mainspring turning. It sounded like the ticking of a clock, or someone typing on a keyboard at a very slow, steady rhythm.
“Then I'll go meet the one who can make the second hand move again.”
「(······Do you truly wish to meet the 'Oldest Dream'?)」
That being was at the terminus of all these stories.
The <Star Stream> had been destroyed, but a question remained.
「Why did a world like this have to exist?」
When I looked back, the others wore similar expressions.
They, too, had problems of their own to resolve and a final act they wanted to see. And to reach it, there was something they had to face.
Yoo Sangah spoke.
“Let's go together, Dokja-ssi.”
“Me, too! I want to go, too!”
“I'm curious what kind of epilogue you wanted to see, ajusshi.”
“Now, now, let's not take this too seriously. We might be surprised to find a kind dokkaebi or something waiting for us. If not, we can make it kind with a few whacks.”
As though agreeing, Biyoo chimed in.
[Baat!]
It was then that Yoo Joonghyuk, who had remained silent, finally spoke.
“Before that, do we have a way to meet it? The Wall is broken, but time has stopped in the outside world. When time stops, Stories cannot move forward. The same must apply to us.”
「(There is a place where time hasn't stopped.)」
Nirvana smiled and pointed at the floor.
That was right. Time had not yet stopped in this 'library'.
“Don't tell me it's inside this library?”
「(······No. This library is only a 'wall', too. But you completed the story, and a passage opened. You can cross to the other side now.)」
With those words, Nirvana led us onward.
For some reason, I thought I knew where they were going.
I remembered the precipice that stretched beneath the library.
「This was the end of the library. The end of every story.」
A fathomless pit. A valley that lay like an abyss.
It was the place I had discovered on the day I first entered the [Fourth Wall].
“······It's that place.”
When I first came here, I had nearly fallen over that precipice.
Nirvana had told me then. Falling down there meant death. Down there was the other side of the Wall.
Nirvana asked.
「(Kim Dokja, do you really want to go?)」
I nodded.
Then Nirvana pulled a rope hanging in midair. Something like a pulley moved, and something like a small elevator slowly rose.
「(Get on.)」
We stepped onto the elevator.
And began descending, little by little.
[Exclusive attribute, 'Looked into the Abyss', is activating.]
The answer I had sought was truly right before me now. The Stories remaining inside me were stirring, too.
How far down had we gone? At last, the pulley fell silent.
When we stepped into the darkness, there was a smell like mold. The floor was slick and damp. It seemed to be the remains of a facility unused for a very long time.
I held the light ahead of us, revealing a faint line of yellow blocks.
“This is······.”

Jung Heewon murmured. A moment later, I heard something rushing through the darkness beyond the yellow blocks. The entire darkness shook ominously. A violent roar, as though a monster were charging toward us.
Soon, the monster's two faint eyes appeared at the far end of the passage.
Jung Heewon, who had murmured, did not reach for her sword even at the sight of the monster. Neither did the others. We all knew what it was.
「The beginning of all these stories.」
A subway train.
The train arrived before us, slowly came to a stop, and opened its doors.
There was no doubt. It was the very subway we knew.
Jung Heewon's lips moved, and she was the first to speak.
“Why on earth is a subway train here······?”
No one could answer that question.
Lee Gilyoung moved first. Yoo Sangah cried out.
“Gilyoung! You can't just get on―”
Lee Gilyoung strode aboard and turned to look at us. The boy shrugged as though nothing were wrong.
Watching him, Lee Jihye took Shin Yoosung's hand and moved.
“Who knows. Let's just get on!”
With that, the others who had been hesitating boarded one by one.
I followed them.
The moment I set foot on the faintly vibrating floor, I felt a sense of déjà vu.
「Once, this had been Kim Dokja's world.」
That was wrong. This was not my world.
「This had been everyone's world.」
Yoo Sangah, Jung Heewon, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye······ Each wore a different expression. I had ridden the subway as part of my daily life, and they must have done much the same.
Some had been office workers, some students, some soldiers, but······.
“The subway······ I used to be so sick of it, but now I'm happy enough to cry.”
At Jung Heewon's words, we slowly looked around the train.
The seats were new, and the handrails were polished clean. There wasn't a trace of filth on the floor.
Of course, what was even more surprising than any of that.
“······But there's nobody here.”
There was no sign of anyone else aboard.
An inorganic space, as though nothing but us was alive. This train held that strange, otherworldly quality.
I turned to the librarians, who were still outside the train, and asked.
“Aren't you coming? You wanted to see the end of the world.”
「(We cannot go.)」
“Why?”
Nirvana and the librarians did not answer. They exchanged strangely sorrowful looks, then spoke.
「(It is enough for us that you see the ending······.)」
[The doors are closing.]
I never heard the rest. The doors closed, and with a sound like enormous wheels turning, the train began to move. Neither fast nor slow. Beyond the windows, the pitch-black scenery crawled past.
I stared into that darkness for a long time. Where on earth was this train going?
“It's Line 3.”
Han Sooyoung had spoken. I looked up at the route map, too.
Line 3. The line I had always taken to and from work. Strangely, the end of the map was damaged. The station names had been erased, too.
The train kept going. Several more minutes passed, but it showed no sign of stopping. It seemed the train would run straight to the terminus.
Han Sooyoung dropped into the seat beside me. Her long lashes fluttered as she glared at the route map. I asked.
“What's with that expression?”
“I don't ride things like the subway.”
“Why?”
I suddenly realized it was a stupid question. Of course someone like her would never need to take the subway. But the words that came from Han Sooyoung were entirely unexpected.
“There's nothing to look at. Inside or outside.”
Together, we looked at the broken route map. True, the subway always ran along the same route. It stopped at the appointed times. Similar things happened against the same scenery, day after day.
I disliked the subway, too. That was much the same reason I had always stared at my smartphone.
“The subway doesn't run to entertain you.”
“······Oh? That doesn't sound like the constellation 'Demon King of Salvation'.”
I smiled bitterly.
Han Sooyoung and I looked in the same direction. The others were there. The people who had endured the apocalypse with me and cleared ninety-nine scenarios to come this far.
“······Um, we're not suddenly going back to the first scenario, are we?”
“No way. Absolutely not!”
“Should I get some grasshoppers ready now?”
The others chuckled at Lee Gilyoung, who clenched his fists with a determined expression.
What did it mean for our most terrible memory to become a joke?
What were they feeling as they smiled at that story?
I spoke to Han Sooyoung.
“They need to return to their ordinary lives.”
“Do you think that will make them happy?”
“That's how every story is supposed to end.”
“Since when did you like that kind of plot?”
Han Sooyoung shot back sarcastically.
“You're not thinking something weird again, are you? You're not hiding something from me again?”
“Even if I wanted to, there's nothing left to hide.”
It was true. Even the original novel had never come this far.
Neither had the 'Secretive Plotter' or the people from the 999th round. We were the first to take this train.
Looking at the blurred, erased end of the route map, I spoke.
“Han Sooyoung, do you think······.”
“Won't there be a final boss after all? That's usually how it goes!”
It was Jung Heewon's voice. She was not speaking to me. The others must have been discussing something among themselves. Shin Yoosung chimed in.
“Or a dragon this big.”
“But I doubt a dragon would have a modifier like 'Oldest Dream'. To have a modifier like that, it would probably have to be······.”
“The 'author', maybe?”
“The author?”
“You know······.”
As Lee Gilyoung, who had brought it up, turned his eyes toward me, the others turned their heads as though they, too, had suddenly remembered.
『Three Ways to Survive in a Ruined World』.
By now, they knew about that novel, too.
They knew that it had contained the story of this world.
And that I alone had read it to the end.
“······What do you think, Dokja-ssi?”
No novel is told before an author writes it.
If this world had been built on 'Ways of Survival', their theory was plausible.
The 'Oldest Dream' was probably the author. I had thought so, too.
But for some reason······.
“I don't think the 'Oldest Dream' is the author of 'Ways of Survival'.”
“Why do you think that?”
“I don't really know why. It's just a feeling.”
I did not think the being at the end of this was tls123.
I remembered the Dokkaebi King's words.
「[The ‘Oldest Dream’ is closer to a reader than an author. That being doesn't write stories for anyone. Too lazy and greedy for that.]」
I also wondered whether any of these theories really needed an 'author' in the first place.
Had this world truly begun because of tls123?
Perhaps tls123 had merely told me about a world that already existed.
Just as the 'Secretive Plotter' and the people of the 999th round, unrecorded on the pages, had existed on their own······.
“Come to think of it, I'm curious. How did you come across that novel, Dokja-ssi?”
“Oh, I've always wondered that, too.”
Even Yoo Joonghyuk, who had been cleaning the [Black Heavenly Demon Sword] as though uninterested, looked my way when the subject came up. Jang Hayoung asked, eyes shining.
“Did you feel some sort of fated attraction?”
“I know that feeling! When I first held a grenade as a private―”
“I just came across it while searching the internet.”
The others looked disappointed by my answer. There was nothing I could do about that. It was the truth. Han Sooyoung scoffed.
“What were you searching for to find a novel like that?”
I couldn't really remember, either.
Lee Jihye shrugged.
“Well, what does that matter now? What matters is that you read it, ajusshi.”
“Exactly. What would we have done if you hadn't read it, Dokja-ssi?”
Looking at Yoo Sangah's beaming face, I shut my mouth.
I had no right to hear those words.
「In the end, the stars fell, and the world's time stopped.」
We were heading toward an ending no one in 'Ways of Survival' had ever reached, but there was no guarantee that what I wanted waited at its end.
From here on, I knew nothing of what would happen, either.
「If someone else had read that novel to the end.」
There were people far better than me. Righteous Jung Heewon, faithful Lee Hyunsung, upright Yoo Sangah. They should have read it to the end. Then this world would have taken a far better shape.
“Thank you, ajusshi. For reading that novel back then.”
Shin Yoosung was smiling, her eyes level with mine.
“That's right. You said the novel wasn't even fun to read, didn't you? If it hadn't been you, Dokja-ssi······.”
“I wouldn't have finished a single page. I really hate books.”
“I tried reading a few books in the barracks library in <Oz>, too······ But reading and I just aren't······.”
Watching Lee Hyunsung scratch his head, I barely managed to close my open mouth.
The people before me now existed because 'Ways of Survival' existed.
Because I had read that novel, I had been able to save them when they were in danger.
Someone as insignificant as me could be loved.
“We came this far because of the Stories you taught us, hyung.”
The children's small hands gripped mine tightly.
I slowly lifted my head. Darkness flowed past the train. Through it passed the Stories we had lived.
We watched those Stories in silence. Beautiful as the Milky Way on a winter night, fleeting as fireworks. Stories no one here could forget, but which would one day be forgotten. Jung Heewon spoke.
“······Dokja-ssi, I think I can ask you now.”
I knew what she would ask.
“What exactly is the 'ending' you wanted?”
There were no constellations watching us now.
The <Star Stream> that had ruled the world was gone, too.
There was no reason I couldn't tell them, either······ probably.
“One of them······ I've already seen.”
I quietly studied each of their faces. No sentences appeared in their expressions. Even so, looking at those faces, I thought I understood what ending I had wanted to see.
“And the other is to repay a debt.”
“A debt?”
When I turned my head, Yoo Joonghyuk was glaring at me.
Rrrrrumble······.
With a heavy vibration, the train gradually began to slow.
We slowly rose. One by one, our noisy companions grew quieter. Tension settled over their faces.
I slowly approached the doors. Jung Heewon stood on my left, Yoo Joonghyuk on my right.
The stream of Stories flowing through the darkness was slowing.
They were not only our stories.
「There was a zeroth round, and there was a first.」
There was a second round, and there was a third.
「Thus, 1,864 rounds gathered together, and those rounds opened this world.」
Countless Yoo Joonghyuks had lived through those rounds. Not one life had been right, but none had been wrong, either.
The world had been too cruel to discuss the ethics of life, and despair too vast to speak of hope. But Yoo Joonghyuk remained steadfast because he never justified himself.
「Only the desire to see the end of this world.」
I had that desire, too.
It was the dream of 1,865 Yoo Joonghyuks, from the zeroth round through the 1,864th.
And the end of this world that I wanted.
“······It's been a long time. Hasn't it?”
Yoo Joonghyuk snapped back as though wondering what I was talking about.
“Only four years, Kim Dokja. Compared to the years I've lived······.”
“Yeah.”
Four years. Before we knew it, that was how long we had fought together.
“Four years that felt like a lifetime.”
Then Jung Heewon, standing on my left, poked me with her sword hilt.
“Why so solemn? We're going to stay together. Don't worry. Whatever monster is waiting, I'll finish it off.”
I smiled quietly. The train slowed further.
My reflection appeared in the black glass of the doors. Blood was smeared across my cheek in the reflection. I wiped the blood off my cheek. And felt a chill.
「It was not on the window. The blood had really been on my cheek.」
“The doors are opening!”
At Lee Hyunsung's shout, everyone readied themselves for battle.
But contrary to our tense expectations, what greeted us was a bare subway platform. People occasionally walked around it, but they did not seem particularly interested in us.
“What? There's nothing······.”

The moment I stepped onto the platform beside the murmuring Jung Heewon, I felt a sense of foreboding. The unfamiliar feel of reality beneath my feet. With faint sparks, every Story I possessed pointed somewhere.
「Someone was sitting on a subway bench.」

A bulky schoolbag stuffed with textbooks, as though its owner had just left school. A short, skinny child sat there. Without the school uniform, I would have thought the child was an elementary schooler.
The boy was drawing something like a chart in his notebook, as though memorizing English vocabulary.
My head throbbed. With difficulty, I forced my unwilling feet to move.
「Kim Dokja had promised. He would end the culprit who had created this world. Whatever that being might be.」
Had someone beaten him somewhere? Dark bruises marked the pale child's arm. Bruises whose origin I felt I knew all too well. My legs went weak, and I could not move.
「Time simply isn't flowing because no one reads or imagines」
I thought this might all be a dream, a lie.
I believed it might be a dream made by the evil <Star Stream>.
But I could not deny it.
Every one of my senses was telling me.
That child was the culprit who had created all these scenarios.
「You ex pected this Kim Dok ja」
The Oldest Dream. A god more omniscient and more incompetent than anyone in the world.
[The influence of the 'Fourth Wall' is gradually weakening.]
「Kim Dok······.」
[The influence of the 'Fourth Wall' is weakening to an extreme degree.]
I heard something fall, then saw Jung Heewon's sword rolling across the floor.
Jung Heewon was looking at me. Eyes that looked at the child, then at me. Despair clouded them.
As though she could not believe it. As though she wished all of this were a lie.
[Your promise to the 'Secretive Plotter' is activating.]
I opened and closed my mouth again and again.
Perhaps this was punishment.
Only now was I paying the price for the salvation I had received.
[You promised to destroy the <Star Stream>.]
[The <Star Stream> will not be destroyed unless the 'Oldest Dream' ends.]
I looked at the child.
A child with exactly the same face as mine.
Slowly, the child raised his head and looked at me.
[End the 'Oldest Dream'.]
My mind kept drifting away.
「What if 'Ways of Survival' were real?」
Was that my thought, or something recorded on the [Final Wall], or neither―
「If there were a world where I could fight alongside the characters of 'Ways of Survival'」
I could not tell whether it was the imagination of the 'Oldest Dream'.
Countless memories surged in like a sudden wave. The imaginings spreading chaotically through a young boy's head became material for stories in other worlds. They became living reality. Tragedy.
